decisions.title: Building regulations
decisions.situation: You stack three blocks. For a moment, the tower stands. Then you discover what your elbow has been planning.

choices.label: Build it again with a wider bottom
Knock down the next tower on purpose
Line the blocks up on the floor

result.title: A better foundation
result.body: The new tower survives your elbow. Your hand brings it down a little later.

journal.text: I rebuilt a block tower with a wider base.

decisions.title: Encore! Encore!
decisions.situation: You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.

result.title: A short, loud career
result.body: You keep banging until you drop the spoon. You look very pleased with yourself.

journal.text: I discovered how much noise a spoon and a bowl could make.

decisions.title: Too busy to be tired
decisions.situation: Sam says it is time for a nap. You have been awake for ages and have only inspected half the room.

choices.label: Give your eyes a short test closure
Ask Sam to stay for a minute
Explain your position at full volume

result.title: Test extended
result.body: You wake up later. The uninspected half of the room is still there.

journal.text: I fell asleep while checking whether I needed a nap.

decisions.title: Customer complaint
decisions.situation: Sam takes you for a haircut. You are convinced the cape means you have been promoted to wizard.

choices.label: Cast a spell on the comb
Ask Sam to hold your hand

result.title: Comb survives
result.body: The comb refuses to turn into a frog. Your haircut carries on.

journal.text: I tried magic during a haircut. It did not affect the comb.

decisions.title: A mouth with sound effects
decisions.situation: Your first loose tooth makes a clicking noise. You discover you can make it louder. Lunch is about to become a performance.

choices.label: Check the wobble in a mirror

result.title: A private dental matter
result.body: You leave the tooth alone. Lunch proceeds without an audience inspecting your mouth.

journal.text: I kept my loose tooth out of the lunchtime conversation.

decisions.title: Birthday invitation
decisions.situation: Avery invites you to a birthday party at an arcade. The invitation has more glitter than useful information.

result.title: Adults need an address
result.body: Sam checks the time and supervision. Their answer and any plan are recorded below. Nothing is paid just for asking.

journal.text: I asked Sam for permission to go to Avery’s arcade birthday.

decisions.title: Party day
decisions.situation: Avery’s arcade birthday is here. Sam agreed to take you. The quoted outing costs $20.00, paid by Sam only if you go.

result.title: High score, low dignity
result.body: You and Avery take turns at the machines. Sam pays the quoted outing cost. Nobody wins enough tickets to retire.

journal.text: I went to Avery’s arcade birthday with Sam.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs $360.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: A disappointing lunch
decisions.situation: Avery opens a lunchbox with nothing in it. They look embarrassed. Sam is nearby.

result.title: Lunch gets sorted
result.body: Sam helps without making an announcement. Avery looks relieved.

journal.text: I quietly got Sam’s help when Avery had no lunch.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Sam’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Sam is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Sam’s mug.

decisions.title: Secrets bingo
decisions.situation: For indoor break, Avery makes bingo cards out of everyone’s embarrassing habits. Your square says “cries at cartoons”. They beg you not to add their baby nickname.

choices.label: Make everyone write their own square
Give a fake sob every time your square comes up
Announce their baby nickname to the room

result.title: Voluntary humiliation
result.body: You admit that cartoon dogs get to you. Someone else confesses to eating a paper cupcake case. Avery quietly removes half the original cards.

journal.text: I turned Avery’s secrets bingo into a game of voluntary confessions.

decisions.title: One star. Still hungry.
decisions.situation: Avery drafts a fake restaurant review of the school canteen. It includes the phrase “structural pasta”.

result.title: Less funny, more useful
result.body: You keep the specific complaints and remove the insults. Alex helps pass it on.

journal.text: I helped Avery turn a canteen rant into useful feedback.

decisions.title: At least you know your name
decisions.situation: Your practice exam is going badly. So far, you have written your name and the date. The date is wrong.

choices.label: Hunt for every easy mark first
Take the wreckage to Alex afterwards
Write an apology in the answer box

result.title: A rescue in small pieces
result.body: You collect enough answers to get moving. Even question one looks less hostile on your second visit.

journal.text: I recovered from freezing in a practice exam by answering easier questions first.

decisions.title: The cable is in your hand
decisions.situation: Sam announces that their charger has been missing for three days. You look down. Their charger is in your hand. There is still time to make this worse.

result.title: Found at the scene
result.body: Sam accepts the charger and your apology. Three days of mystery ends in approximately two seconds.

journal.text: I returned Sam’s charger and admitted forgetting about it.

decisions.title: You are in verse two
decisions.situation: Avery asks you to help rehearse a song about everyone who has annoyed them. Your name appears in verse two. The rhyme is frankly weak.

choices.label: Suggest a better rhyme for your insult
Ask why you made the track list

result.title: An unwilling co-writer
result.body: You improve the line and rehearse the chorus. Avery laughs, then admits that your original offence was borrowing a pencil.

journal.text: I helped Avery rehearse a song that included an insult about me.

decisions.title: The Biscuit Bandit speaks
decisions.situation: For a family-history assignment, you ask Sam about school. They admit their nickname was “The Biscuit Bandit”, then ask whether the interview is being recorded.

choices.label: Ask for a version safe to hand in
Keep interrupting to demand biscuit details

result.title: A surprisingly large operation
result.body: The story involves a lunch tin and a very unconvincing alibi. You organise the useful parts into your assignment. Sam enjoys telling you the rest.

journal.text: I interviewed Sam about their childhood nickname.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: The plan met a different day
decisions.situation: While living with Asthma, you reach an optional household task with less energy than you expected. Yesterday’s plan did not allow for that.

choices.label: Choose a smaller version of the task
Leave the optional task and rest
Push through to satisfy the old plan

result.title: A plan that can bend
result.body: You do one manageable part and leave the rest. An incomplete chore feels less important once it stops being a test.

journal.text: I adjusted an optional task to the energy I had with Asthma.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. You have been diagnosed with Asthma. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs $360.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. You have been diagnosed with Asthma. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs $360.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Sam sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Save a copy and label it

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Sam remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Sam also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Chicago, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Chicago.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Change your position and relax your shoulders

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Chicago unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Hear the allegedly deceased man out

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Chicago.

decisions.title: A number with nowhere to go
decisions.situation: You suddenly remember a telephone number you have not used for years. You cannot remember what you entered a room to fetch, but the number is perfect.

choices.label: Return calmly to the original task
Treat the distraction as a personal crisis

result.title: An impressive useless recital
result.body: You repeat the number once and laugh at the timing. Memory has supplied an answer to a question nobody asked.

journal.text: I remembered an old telephone number at an unhelpful moment.

decisions.title: What do you do all day?
decisions.situation: A stranger assumes you are retired and asks whether you have taken up “something gentle, like birdwatching”. You have not told them anything about your life.

choices.label: Tell them what your days actually involve
Say the birds are frightened of you
Describe every activity they failed to imagine

result.title: An overdue factual check
result.body: You give a short answer. They apologise for inventing your schedule before learning your name.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger’s assumption about my daily life.

decisions.title: Beginners’ self-defence
decisions.situation: At a free beginner lesson, the instructor asks you to demonstrate a firm “No!” You give one so convincing that a passer-by apologises and leaves.

choices.label: Practise the rest of the lesson
Use your new “No!” on the whole lesson

result.title: A useful loud afternoon
result.body: You learn the basics and repeat the shout. The corridor remains unusually clear for the rest of the lesson.

journal.text: I practised the basics at a free self-defence lesson.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.
